partners.mechanism_chain: ATP7B (HGNC:830) —DISRUPTS→ copper transport and ceruloplasmin metabolism (GO:0005374); copper transport and ceruloplasmin metabolism (GO:0005374) —LEADS_TO→ hepatic dysfunction (HP:0001375); ATP2B3 (HGNC:10476) —DISRUPTS→ calcium homeostasis (GO:0005509); calcium homeostasis (GO:0005509) —DISRUPTS→ intracellular calcium levels (CHEBI:26397); intracellular calcium levels (CHEBI:26397) —LEADS_TO→ cerebellar ataxia (HP:0001251); ATP7B (HGNC:830) —DISRUPTS→ ATP hydrolysis (GO:0004098); ATP2B3 (HGNC:10476) —DISRUPTS→ ATP hydrolysis (GO:0004098); ATP hydrolysis (GO:0004098) —LEADS_TO→ calcium homeostasis (GO:0005509). Loss-of-function mutations in ATP7B disrupt copper transport and ceruloplasmin metabolism, leading to hepatic dysfunction in Wilson disease. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in ATP2B3 disrupt calcium homeostasis, causing cerebellar ataxia in X-linked progressive cerebellar ataxia. partners.mechanism_chain: ATP7B (HGNC:717) —DISRUPTS→ copper transport and homeostasis (GO:0006821); copper transport and homeostasis (GO:0006821) —LEADS_TO→ hepatic copper accumulation (HP:0001395); ATP2A2 (HGNC:712) —DISRUPTS→ calcium homeostasis (GO:0005488); calcium homeostasis (GO:0005488) —DISRUPTS→ protein folding (GO:0006457); protein folding (GO:0006457) —DISRUPTS→ ER-associated degradation (GO:0030437); ER-associated degradation (GO:0030437) —LEADS_TO→ keratosis (HP:0000957). Loss-of-function mutations in ATP7B disrupt copper transport, leading to its accumulation and subsequent liver damage (Wilson disease). Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in ATP2A2 impair SERCA pump activity, destabilizing calcium homeostasis. This disruption affects various cellular processes, including protein folding and ER-associated degradation, ultimately contributing to epidermal abnormalities like keratosis (Darier disease). The convergence point is the cellular machinery for protein homeostasis, which is sensitive to both copper dysregulation and calcium imbalance.
